purpose: rows needing a bilingual read before they can be served. SPANISH FIRST -- es-419 is what the Mexican partner pulls. No instrument here can check these: the leak index is English ISO text, so every row below scores zero before and after. What is being looked for is ISO's own Spanish or Portuguese sentence reproduced in a translation, which only a reader with the standard can see.

english_spans.after: is essential to developing and using an AI system responsibly, and names

entries.note: restatement of Annex D.2

english_spans.before: Conformity generates evidence of the organization's responsibility and accountability regarding its role with respect to AI systems, which is
english_spans.after: Conformity generates evidence that the organization is responsible and accountable for whatever role it holds around AI systems, which is

entries.note: the conformity-evidence phrasing, which recurs at 5.5

english_spans.before: span risk management, impact assessment, resource management, security, safety, privacy, development, performance, human oversight, supplier relationships and data quality across
english_spans.after: span impact assessment, security, privacy, safety, data quality, development, performance, supplier relationships, resource management, risk management and human oversight across

entries.note: A LIST. The run was ISO's ordering and nothing else; reordering changes no meaning.

english_spans.before: clause 6.1.4 states that the organization shall consider the results of the AI system impact assessment in the risk assessment, with
english_spans.after: clause 6.1.4 requires the impact assessment's results to be taken into account when risk is assessed, with

entries.note: clause 6.1.4 quoted with `shall`; the modal is held as `requires`

english_spans.before: Documented information must be available to the extent necessary to have confidence that processes were carried out as planned.
english_spans.after: Documented information must be kept to whatever extent gives confidence that the processes ran as planned.

entries.note: clause 7.5 documented-information phrasing

english_spans.before: or an entire AI system for use on its own or as part of another product.
english_spans.after: or an entire AI system, whether it is used standalone or embedded in another product.

entries.note: the supplier-scope phrasing

english_spans.before: AI risk assessments are performed at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur. The
english_spans.after: AI risk assessments are performed at planned intervals, and again whenever a significant change is proposed or occurs. The

english_spans.before: AI system impact assessments are performed at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed to occur.
english_spans.after: AI system impact assessments run on the same trigger: planned intervals, plus any significant change that is proposed.

entries.note: the planned-intervals phrasing, TWICE -- once for risk assessments, once for impact assessments

english_spans.before: not all are required to be used, and the organization can design and implement its own.
english_spans.after: not every control must be used, and an organization may design and implement its own.

english_spans.before: though organizations do not have to document or justify inclusion or exclusion of the implementation guidance in the Statement of Applicability
english_spans.after: though an organization is not required to document or justify which parts of that guidance it adopted in the Statement of Applicability

entries.note: two runs: the Annex A optionality sentence and the Annex B documentation sentence

english_spans.before: Organizations may not require all controls listed in Annex A, and may exceed that list with
english_spans.after: An organization may need only some of the Annex A controls, and may go beyond that list with

entries.note: the SoA scope phrasing

english_spans.before: documenting a policy for the development or use of AI systems, determining
english_spans.after: documenting a policy covering how AI systems get developed or used, determining

english_spans.before: putting in place a process to report concerns about the organization's role with respect to an AI system, and
english_spans.after: putting in place a route for raising concerns about whatever role the organization holds around a given AI system, and

entries.note: two runs: the AI policy phrase and control A.3.3's concern-reporting route

english_spans.before: determine at which phases of the life cycle record keeping of event logs should be enabled, with
english_spans.after: determine at which life-cycle phases event logs should be kept, with

entries.note: ISO says logging SHOULD be enabled. The first draft wrote `must`, which invents an obligation. The weak modal is held.

english_spans.before: between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties, establish
english_spans.after: between the organization and its suppliers, partners, customers and other third parties, establish

entries.note: A LIST. Reordered; no meaning changes.

english_spans.before: It must evaluate the performance and the effectiveness of the AI management system.
english_spans.after: It must evaluate how well the AI management system performs and how effective it is.

english_spans.before: records that performance refers both to results achieved by using AI systems and results related to the management system itself, and
english_spans.after: records that performance covers two things at once: what using the AI systems achieves, and how the management system itself is doing, and

entries.note: two runs: the clause 9.1 evaluation duty and the note to the performance definition

english_spans.before: and considers the importance of the processes concerned and the results of previous audits. The organization defines
english_spans.after: and weighs how important the processes under audit are, together with what earlier audits found. The organization defines

english_spans.before: selects auditors and conducts audits to ensure objectivity and the impartiality of the audit process, and ensures
english_spans.after: selects auditors and runs audits in a way that keeps the process objective and impartial, and ensures

entries.note: two runs: the audit-programme inputs and the auditor-selection sentence

english_spans.before: Top management reviews the AIMS at planned intervals to ensure its continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness.
english_spans.after: Top management reviews the AIMS at planned intervals, checking that it still suits the organization, is still adequate and still works.

english_spans.before: Results include decisions related to continual improvement opportunities and any need for changes to the AIMS, and
english_spans.after: Results record what was decided about improvement opportunities and about any changes the AIMS needs, and

entries.note: two runs: the review trigger and the management-review outputs

english_spans.before: to eliminate the causes so that it does not recur or occur elsewhere, by reviewing
english_spans.after: to eliminate the causes, so the same failure does not come back or turn up somewhere else, by reviewing

english_spans.before: documented information must be available as evidence of the nature of the nonconformities, subsequent actions taken and the results of corrective action
english_spans.after: documented information must be kept showing what the nonconformities were, what was done about them, and what the corrective action achieved

entries.note: two runs: clause 10.2's recurrence phrase and its documented-information phrase

english_spans.before: ISO/IEC 17021-1, the generic requirements for bodies providing audit and certification of management systems.
english_spans.after: ISO/IEC 17021-1, which states the requirements a certification body must meet when it audits and certifies management systems.

english_spans.before: conforming with its requirements can generate evidence of its responsibility and accountability regarding its role with respect to AI systems, which is
english_spans.after: conforming with its requirements can produce evidence that it is responsible and accountable for whatever role it holds around AI systems, which is

entries.note: two runs: the 17021-1 title and the same conformity-evidence phrasing as 1.5
